process_observations.observation: Every cross-step reference this rule needs was already on disk and resolved on the first attempt: the Tier_2_Engineering queue, the case_intake/Case_Escalated_To_Tier2 Classic template, and the Severity 1 picklist value.

The M3-S02 email template's own description names this exact consumer - 'the assignedToTemplate on the 8-business-hour Case escalation action (M4-S04)' - so the template reference was read off an upstream artefact rather than assumed.

The plan's own step note predicted both checker constraints (E2 on a businessHours child under a Case source, E7 on a label-form assignedTo) and both were avoided by construction; the checker exited 0 on the first pass at both scopes with no repair.

notifyCaseOwner true resolves at run time to the queue that owns the case, and the Billing queue's notification address is billing@acme.example - a live Email-to-Case intake address - so an escalation notification on a Billing-owned case becomes a new case that escalates and notifies again.

Entry 2 reads Case.BusinessHoursId, and the step that populates it (M4-S03) is not built; no skill states what businessHoursSource Case does when that reference is null, so the weekend pause requirement.md L16 promises is unproven until M4-S03 ships.

As built under Q42 (CaseCreation, disableEscalationWhenModified false) a case an agent is actively working still escalates 480 minutes after creation, which is narrower than requirement.md L16's word 'untouched'.

No source gives Severity 1 a threshold of its own: requirement.md L16 states one threshold and L18 says only that Severity 1 never pauses, so both entries carry 480 and differ only in clock source - a shorter Severity 1 value would have been an invented SLA.

No file in the library shows a custom field inside an escalation-rule criteriaItems; Case.Severity__c composes the escalation skill's Case. prefix with the Object.Field__c form documented in six other admin skills, and is marked UNVERIFIED rather than treated as quoted.
The step's declared checker and its manifest and XML checks are the tester's to run, not this agent's.

process_observations.observation: The flywheel ran as designed for the second time in this milestone: the org's rejection became checker rule E10, a gotcha with the exact error text and an anti-pattern entry, so the constraint is now caught locally before a deploy rather than by a deploy.

The first build was not refutable from the library: at v1.1.1 every worked example in the cited skill wrote notifyCaseOwner with no notifyToTemplate, and the Metadata API guide's EscalationAction table marks the element optional, so the shape the org rejects was the shape the skill taught.

The launch instruction said Q45 names the escalation template; Q45 names no template, and the value was resolved from M3-S02's declared outputs instead - the same template, a different source, recorded rather than silently reconciled.
Adding notifyToTemplate did not narrow the R2 Billing mail-loop exposure - it made the mail R2 describes actually send, because notifyToTemplate addresses the same recipient notifyCaseOwner selects.
